rationale: A generic germ-cell/teratoma descriptor (British testicular teratoma terminology) that occurs across many midline and gonadal sites; within this ceiling it is not restricted to a defined proper subset.

Papillary craniopharyngioma arises from craniopharyngeal-duct (Rathke pouch) epithelial remnants in the sellar/suprasellar-infundibulotuberal region, occupying both the pituitary (C751) and craniopharyngeal duct (C752) codes; not restricted to a proper subset of its 2-code ceiling.
Synonym of craniopharyngioma, papillary; a craniopharyngeal-duct/sellar tumor occupying both C751 and C752, so not restricted to a proper subset of its ceiling.

Pituicytoma arises specifically from pituicytes of the neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) and infundibulum, i.e. the pituitary gland (C751); it does not originate from craniopharyngeal-duct/Rathke remnants (C752), so it is restricted to a proper subset of its ceiling.

An obscure/archaic neuroblastic term with insufficient dedicated modern literature to establish a specific anatomic restriction; while neuroblastic tumors favor adrenal and sympathetic paraganglia/retroperitoneal sites, a defensible strict subset of this ceiling could not be verified from a fetched source.
